sentences.text: 4. The claim petition was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for brevity 'the Act') claiming an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 07.09.2006.
6. The respondent Nos.1 and 2 i.e., driver and owner of the offending motorcycle remained ex parte before the Tribunal.

7. The respondent No.3/Insurance Company filed counter contending that the claimant shall prove the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the respondent No.1; the particulars of the offending motorcycle and the vehicle of the insured was not informed to the respondent No.3/Insurance Company; the owner and insurer of the vehicle of the claimant were not implicated as parties to the petition and the compensation claimed by the claimant is excessive.

sentences.text:
The learned Tribunal, basing on the rival contentions, framed the following issues for trial:
1. Whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to claim compensation.

If so, from which of the respondents?
3.
Whether the claim sought for by the petitioner and the interest are excessive?

4. To what relief?
9. During enquiry, on behalf of claimant, the claimant examined himself as P.W.1.
The Doctor, who treated P.W.1, was examined as P.W.2 and the rider of the motorcycle, on which the claimant travelled at the time of accident, was examined as P.W.3.
Besides that the claimant got exhibited Ex.A1 to Ex.A8 and Ex.X1 documents.
No evidence was adduced on behalf of the respondent No.3/Insurance Company, except filing Ex.B1, copy of policy relating to the offending motorcycle.

10. The learned Tribunal, basing on the above evidence, considered the issue Nos.1 to 3, but answered the issues MACMA No.1820 of 2012 BVLNC, J Date 16.02.2024 Nos.1 only holding that there is a material contradiction with regard to the date of accident mentioned in the petition and the evidence placed before the Tribunal and therefore, hold that the claimant failed to prove the accident and 'Dismissed' the claim petition.
The Tribunal did not answer the issue No.3 holding that in view of the finding in issue Nos.1 and 2, issue No.3 need not be answered.
It is pertinent to note down that issue No.3 relates to assessment of compensation entitled by the claimant.

11. The learned counsel for the claimant would submit that the Tribunal without properly considering the evidence placed before it, came to an erroneous opinion that the claimant failed to prove that accident was occurred and he sustained injuries in the said accident.

He would further submit that the learned Tribunal merely basing on a date mentioned in the petition as date of accident, came to a conclusion that no accident was occurred without perusing Ex.X1, FIR and the evidence of P.W.1/claimant and the evidence of Doctor and P.W.3 about the date of accident and the manner in which the accident was occurred; and MACMA No.1820 of 2012 BVLNC, J Date 16.02.2024 therefore, the order and decree of the learned Tribunal is not sustainable in law.
12.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.3/ Insurance Company would submit that admittedly, the date of accident is mentioned as '07.09.2006' in the claim petition; whereas, as per Ex.A1/FIR, the accident was occurred on 20.08.2006 and therefore, the learned Tribunal came to right conclusion that the claimant failed to prove the occurrence of accident, and therefore, there are no grounds to interfere with the finding of the learned Tribunal.
13.

Considering the rival contentions, the points that would arise for consideration in this appeal are as under:

2. To what relief?
 MACMA No.1820 of 2012 BVLNC, J Date 16.02.2024 POINT N O.1:
14.

The case of the claimant as per the claim petition, on 06.09.2006 the claimant was travelling as pillion-rider on a motorcycle to attend a function, going to Adavuladeevi of Repalle Mandal; on the way, when they reached a place in Minenivaripalem, the motorcycle on which the claimant was travelling, fell into a ditch; then, the offending motorcycle driven by the respondent No.1 coming behind,
negligently dashed the motorcycle on which the claimant was travelling; as a result,
the claimant fell down and sustained injuries; immediately, the claimant was shifted to the hospital in Repalle, where First-Aid was given to him; later, he was shifted to Lalitha Super speciality Hospital, Guntur for better treatment.

The claimant examined himself as P.W.1.
15.
In the chief-examination affidavit, he stated that on 20.08.2006 he was travelling on the motorcycle.
Except the date, remaining facts, the way in which the accident was occurred are tallying with the facts mentioned in the petition.

The learned Tribunal while answering the issue MACMA No.1820 of 2012 BVLNC, J Date 16.02.2024 whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending motorcycle, found that as per the evidence, the accident was occurred on '20.08.2006';
whereas, the date is mentioned as '06.09.2006' in the pleading and the claimant did not take any steps to amend the petition and that, FIR was registered on 07.09.2006 and delay was not properly explained by the claimant and in view of the said contradictions, came to a conclusion that the claimant failed to establish that the accident was occurred and sustained injuries in the said accident.
16. The Tribunal while considering the evidence of claimant, the P.W.2/Doctor and P.W.3, failed to consider the contents of Ex.A1/FIR, except stating that it was registered on '07.09.2006'.
The contents of Ex.A.1/FIR would establish that the accident was occurred on '20.08.2006'.
17. It is pertinent to note down that the statement basing on which FIR was registered is of the wife of the injured.

A close scrutiny of Ex.A1/FIR would disclose that the Guntur Police was intimated by Vissamsetty Harikrishna vs Samarla Venkaga Suresh Babu 2 Ors on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37807743/

sentences.text: the hospital about the accident on MACMA No.1820 of 2012 BVLNC, J Date 16.02.2024 '21.08.2006' through 'MLC (Medico-Legal Case)' intimation.
It would also disclose that the Guntur police went to the hospital on that day, but could not record the statement of injured as he was not in a position to make statement.
18. The evidence of P.W.2/Doctor would disclose that the injured suffered fracture of skull.
It appears that on account of the said head injury, he was suffering from temporary loss of memory and therefore, he was not in a position to make any statement.
As rightly found in Ex.A1/FIR, the police could able to record the statement of wife of the injured on 28.08.2006 in the hospital at Guntur.
Later, it was forwarded to Repalle police on 06.09.2006 and then, Repalle police registered the FIR under Ex.A1 on 07.09.2006.

So, all these facts and circumstances were found in Ex.A1/FIR and the evidence of P.W.2/Doctor also discloses that the injured was admitted in the hospital soon after the accident on 21.08.2006 at Guntur.

19. It is pertinent to note down that immediately after the accident, the claimant was taken to hospital at Repalle and then, he was again taken to Lalitha Super Speciality MACMA No.1820 of 2012 BVLNC, J Date 16.02.2024 Hospital at Guntur for better case management.

sentences.text: When all these facts and circumstances manifest that accident was occurred on 20.08.2006 evening and then, the injured was shifted to nearby hospital in Repalle and from there, he was shifted to Guntur and admitted on 21.08.2006 and then, police went there, but could not record his statement immediately, as he was not in a position to make any statement due to head injury and then, they found the wife of the injured and as such, they recorded her statement on 20.08.2006.
Then, it was forwarded to Repalle police station on point of jurisdiction and it was registered as FIR on 07.09.2006.
Under those circumstances, it appears that inadvertently, due to typographical mistake the date of accident was mentioned on 07.09.2006 i.e., date of registration of FIR, in the claim petition.
20. The learned Tribunal unfortunately failed to consider the above facts and circumstances, and casually considered the dates only, but not the facts.

Thereby came to an erroneous conclusion that the claimant failed to prove that the accident was occurred and claimant sustained injuries MACMA No.1820 of 2012 BVLNC, J Date 16.02.2024 in the accident.
Therefore, the finding of the learned Tribunal is liable to be set-aside.
21. As already stated above, the learned Tribunal not answered the issue No.3 on the ground that the accident was not proved.
In law, the learned Tribunal is expected to answer all the issues irrespective of the finding on issue Nos.1 and 2.
But, the Tribunal failed to discharge its duty answering issue No.3.
In that view of the matter, the matter has to be remitted to the Tribunal for considering issue Nos.2 and 3 also which relates to the quantum of compensation and the interest claimed by the claimant.
Accordingly, point No.1 is answered.

POINT N O.2:
22.
In the light of finding on point No.1, the appeal in M.A.C.M.A.No.1820 of 2012 is liable to be 'Remitted to the Tribunal with a direction for fresh disposal'.
